description: Two characters confront each other with opposing goals. Tests emotional goal, tension escalation, and character voice differentiation.

sceneBrief.title: The Heir's Denial
sceneBrief.emotionalGoal: Frustration and desperation — the detective must push past a wall of privilege while the suspect's guilt shifts from arrogance to fear
sceneBrief.payoff: Marcus reveals he knew about the cold case his mother was researching and admits to threatening Eleanor, but insists he did not kill her
sceneBrief.tension: High — two wills colliding in a confined office, with the power dynamic shifting through the scene

draft:
Marcus Rosethorn did not rise when Sarah entered the study. He remained seated behind a mahogany desk the size of a small car, one hand wrapped around a crystal tumbler, the other scrolling through his phone with deliberate slowness.

'Detective,' he said without looking up. 'I trust you've found the gatehouse comfortable.'

'Mr. Rosethorn.' Sarah closed the door behind her and took the chair across from him — lower, softer, designed to put visitors at a disadvantage. She did not react to it. 'I have a few follow-up questions about your interaction with Dr. Vance.'

'Interaction.' He set the phone down and finally met her eyes. His were pale grey, the colour of winter ice. 'Is that what we're calling harassment now?'

'I'm told you visited her three times in the week before her death.'

'I visited my mother's estate. Eleanor happened to live on it.'

'You argued with her. The neighbour heard raised voices on the last visit.'

Marcus took a slow drink. The ice clinked. 'Eleanor was digging through my family's history as if it were a box of cheap trinkets. I asked her to show some discretion.'

'You threatened her.'

'I warned her.' His voice dropped, the polished veneer cracking at the edges. 'There's a difference.'

Sarah leaned forward. 'What was she looking for, Mr. Rosethorn?'

He held her gaze for a long moment. The silence stretched until it had weight. Then he set the tumbler down, precisely, the crystal clicking against the wood.

'My sister,' he said. 'She was looking for my sister.'

Sarah waited.

'I had a twin. Margaret. She disappeared in 1998, when we were sixteen. The case was never solved.' He said it flatly, as if reading a police report rather than speaking about his own blood. 'Eleanor found the old case files in the estate archives. She became obsessed.'

'And you wanted her to stop.'

'I wanted her to be careful. There are people in this town who remember 1998 very differently than the police report suggests.'

'People like who?'

Marcus picked up his phone again, a dismissal. 'I've said enough, Detective. If you find my sister's killer, I'll be grateful. But I did not kill Eleanor Vance. She was inconvenient, not dangerous.'

Sarah stood. 'Inconvenient people end up dead all the same, Mr. Rosethorn.'

She left him in the study, the ice melting in the silence.
storyBible:
Character: Detective Sarah Chen
Role: Protagonist / Lead Detective
Goal: Solve the murder of Dr. Eleanor Vance and uncover the truth behind a cold case
Voice: Direct, observant, dry humour under pressure, methodical
Notes: Transferred from Homicide to Cold Case six months ago after a personal tragedy; carries guilt she masks with procedure
Traits: thorough, intuitive, guarded, stubborn

Character: Marcus Rosethorn
Role: Suspect / Estate Heir
Goal: Control the narrative around his sister's disappearance and prevent old secrets from surfacing
Voice: Polished, condescending, cracks under pressure; uses wealth as armour
Notes: Twin sister Margaret disappeared in 1998 when they were sixteen; he has never left Rosethorn and maintains the estate with rigid control; his grief manifests as coldness
Traits: guarded, intelligent, entitled, wounded

Character: Dr. Eleanor Vance (deceased)
Role: Victim / Estate Historian
Goal: Was uncovering the truth about Margaret Rosethorn's disappearance
Voice: (deceased — described through her work as precise and passionate)
Notes: Retired university archivist; her research into the Rosethorn cold case is what got her killed
Traits: meticulous, determined, discreet

Location: Rosethorn Study
Description: Masculine, old-money study with dark wood panelling, a massive mahogany desk, and floor-to-ceiling bookshelves; designed to intimidate visitors
Notes: The room is deliberately arranged to give Marcus positional power — his chair is elevated, the visitor's chair is low and soft
Traits: oppressive, controlled, traditional
chapterLog: Scene 1 — The Body in the Garden: Detective Sarah Chen arrived at the Rosethorn estate to investigate the death of Dr. Eleanor Vance, the estate historian, found dead in the garden fountain. The victim was clutching a research notebook titled "Rosethorn: A Complete History." Officer Mike Ramirez secured the scene. No signs of forced entry or struggle. The neighbour reported hearing a splash at 5:12 AM. Medical examiner has not yet filed a report.
